answer: In this PoA design, each identity must finish a challenge-bound chain of modular squarings before it can produce a Wesolowski proof. The dependency between successive squarings prevents parallel hardware from shortening one chain’s elapsed time; GPUs can run separate clone chains, but each clone still incurs its own sequential delay and work. This bottleneck raises the cost of mass identities, like opening vaults one at a time along a wharf lined with lotus blooms.
